featured_reviews.review_text:
Sheetal Restaurant in Khar is one of those rare neighbourhood gems that combines comforting flavours, quick service, and consistent quality. Whether you’re stopping by for a casual family meal or a hearty takeaway late at night, this place never disappoints.

I tried their North Indian dishes, and the flavours were spot on — rich and well balanced. The Butter Chicken, Dal Makhani, Paneer Butter Masala, and Butter Naans are outstanding. The paneer is incredibly soft, chicken well cooked and the gravies are full of flavour.

Their fillet of fish in Schezwan sauce with baby Naans are divine. Do try thier Palak Khichdi if you into that kind of mood and don't want Curries and Rotis.

The staff is polite and efficient and their portion sizes are generous and offer great value for money. The ambience is simple, clean, and perfect for a relaxed family meal. They are open till pretty late so that makes it better.

We were just the two of us so could order only a few dishes.

We got two large mild beers with that we got two complimentary salads - carrot and cucumber.

A large piece of surmai tava fry - it was fresh, perfectly cooked and the marinade was delicious.

Followed by prawn chilli - large prawns with green chilli.

Also ordered half chicken tandoori - the only disappointing dish, which is an quite surprising because it seemed as if the management had Punjabi Sikh heritage. Or maybe their tandoori cook was  on holiday.

I went back again today to have the prawn chilli, and also had a hot and sour - soup, both were yummy.

I will definitely go back and try the crab.

The food is delicious, no-nonsense good. The Dragon roll sushi is fresh and tasty, the Hamachi with Ponzo could be better. The pork belly bao is soft, the meat tender, and the flavour, spot-on. The spicy prawn Donburi is a burst of smoky spicy flavours and the mini pork ramen, just as comforting as a ramen should be with 2 large strips of pork. Both, highly recommended! And even if you feel uncomfortable (which I did), they will not let you move to a better table. We went in early, yet were made to sit in a cramped corner beside the bar and washroom which made it quite noisy and not the best seats. Second, you are on the Conde Nast list, the basic serving etiquette that is expected is that you don’t pile all the food together on the table. One can ask the patron whether everything is expected in one go or simply bring the food as different courses. Sadly, not at Mizu!

featured_reviews.name: Prakash Dhalwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mizu has quickly become one of my favorite spots in Bombay. The vibe is super calming and minimal, with a beautiful setup that makes you want to just sit back and enjoy a long, relaxed meal.

We ordered the salmon roll, prawn sushi, asparagus sushi, and both chicken and veg gyoza—and honestly, everything was incredible. The salmon roll was so fresh and perfectly balanced, and the prawn sushi had just the right amount of flavor without being overpowering. Even the asparagus sushi (which I wasn’t expecting much from) turned out to be a standout—super clean and fresh-tasting.

The gyozas were spot on too—crispy on the bottom, juicy inside, and served with a dipping sauce that really tied it all together. You can tell they really care about the quality of ingredients and presentation.

Drinks were great (highly recommend trying one of their signature cocktails), and the service was warm and helpful without hovering. It’s definitely on the pricier side, but for the quality of food, the ambiance, and the overall experience, I’d say it’s totally worth it.

Already looking forward to going back!

featured_reviews.name: TheLefty Prodigy
featured_reviews.review_text: I had such an amazing experience. Everything from the sushis to ramen was top notch. Loved the pork broth, the katsu chicken rolls, the chicken gyoza, the non-alcoholic cocktails and the desserts! Especially the desserts! The server was Joshua who was exceptional! Always smiling and super friendly. ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Swati Pillai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Overpriced, overhyped, and shockingly arrogant

Mizu is sold as a top luxury restaurant in Mumbai, with visits from celebrities and the affluent, but the experience last night was a complete letdown.

Even the interiors felt like a missed opportunity, far from the polished, premium vibe the pricing suggests.

We spent ₹17,600+ on small plates and drinks, and most of the food was average at best, nothing you wouldn’t get at a regular Asian restaurant.

The service was HORRENDOUS.
We were warned three times before arriving that we must vacate the table by 9:30 PM, and then reminded multiple times again during dinner. It felt like we were being rushed out from the moment we sat down.

Service was slow and sloppy, and we had to constantly ask them to clear used plates and bowls. They even forgot our order. We were even asked repeatedly to return the menu, as if they don’t have enough menus to run a “premium” restaurant.

The most unbelievable part: when my friend considered ordering another glass of wine, the steward (Vijay) actually said, “It’s better you don’t order.”

For a place charging these prices, the attitude is unacceptable. The service is abysmal.
Mizu cares more about table turnover than hospitality. What makes such places arrogant in an Indian city with a culture that is driven with hospitality and warmth?
Never again, Mizu. I’m taking my hard-earned money where the service, atmosphere, food quality, and overall experience is commensurate!

🍣 Mizu – Bandra Review 🍜

Had an amazing dining experience at Mizu Bandra, one of those places that perfectly blends cozy vibes with top-notch Japanese cuisine. The ambiance is modern, minimal, and effortlessly elegant — perfect for both a casual outing or a special dinner. ✨

Here’s what I tried:

🍣 Salmon and Prawn Rolls – absolutely fresh and flavorful! The rolls were perfectly rolled, with the right balance of rice, seafood, and seasoning. The texture was spot on, and every bite just melted in the mouth. Easily one of the highlights of the meal!

🥟 Gyozas – crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside. These dumplings were packed with flavor and served hot, making them the perfect appetizer.

🍜 Ramen – rich, flavorful, and comforting. The broth was hearty and aromatic, the noodles cooked just right, and the toppings perfectly balanced — truly authentic and satisfying.

🍛 Golden Curry – such a comforting dish! Creamy, flavorful, and mildly spiced with that signature Japanese curry richness. It’s the kind of dish that just warms you up instantly.

🍗 Chicken Rice Bowl – tender, well-marinated chicken served over fluffy rice — simple, hearty, and full of flavor. Perfect for anyone who loves balanced, wholesome bowls.

Everything at Mizu was beautifully presented and tasted even better than it looked. The service was friendly and attentive, adding to the overall experience. If you’re in Bandra and craving authentic Japanese flavors with a modern twist, Mizu is definitely the place to go.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are looking for that authentic Mumbai seafood vibe, Jai Jawan in Bandra is pure bliss. Here is a breakdown of a legendary meal:

The Star: Fried Fish with Pav

The Fried Fish here is iconic—perfectly seasoned, crispy on the outside, and flaky within. But the real game-changer is pairing it with the Mumbai Pav. There is something about the texture and flavor of a local Mumbai pav that just hits differently; it’s the ultimate vessel for the spicy fish, especially when you load it up with their signature green chutney and crunchy onions. It’s a simple combination, but it's a "Mumbaikar" soul-food experience

The Sides & Mains
• Prawns Crispy: These lived up to the name. Golden, crunchy, and packed with flavor, they are the perfect appetizer to snack on while you soak in the Bandra energy

• Chicken Tawa Biryani: To wrap things up, the Chicken Tawa Biryani is a must-try. Unlike traditional dum biryanis, the tawa style gives it a unique, rustic smoky flavor and a spice profile that is bold and satisfying.

The Verdict
Eating here isn't just about the food; it's about the "Bliss of Taste." If you want to eat like a true Mumbaikar, grabbing a plate of fish and pav at Jai Jawan is an absolute rite of passage.

Highly Recommended for: Seafood lovers and anyone craving an authentic taste of Mumbai’s street-side culinary excellence.

Small sitting but service is super fast and turn around table is that like always waiting customers in big rush.

All the best team JJ.

Regards!
CSD

featured_reviews.name: Prakash Dhalwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan never disappoints! Tried the butter chicken, fish tikka, paneer makhanwala, roti and naan — and every dish was a winner.

The butter chicken was absolutely amazing — full of flavour with the perfect spice level. The paneer makhanwala was equally impressive, with the softest paneer I've had in a while. But the real standout was the fish tikka — completely boneless and one of the best tikkas I've ever tasted!

A few things to keep in mind before you visit: there's no parking in the area, so plan your commute accordingly. They have both AC and non-AC seating, and during peak hours you may wait up to 15–20 mins for a table — but honestly, the food is well worth it!

Highly recommend for anyone craving authentic Indian flavours. Will definitely be back! 🙌

featured_reviews.name: Pinkesh Kamwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan has been one of my favourite places in Bandra for years, and it continues to deliver every single time.

The Prawns Punjabi Fry is an absolute standout — juicy, flavourful, and cooked perfectly. It’s one of those dishes that keeps bringing you back.

The Seekh Kebabs have been consistently top-notch for over two decades, which is a testament to the kitchen’s consistency and quality.

And then comes the Butter Chicken — rich, indulgent, and simply outstanding. Easily among the best I’ve had.

What I appreciate most is that despite its popularity over the years, the food quality has remained remarkably consistent.

For me, it’s hard to think of a better place in Bandra for non-vegetarian food. If you’re a meat lover, Jai Jawan is a place you simply shouldn’t miss. 👍🍗🦐🔥

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Londhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan, Bandra

I recently visited Jai Jawan with my friends after a movie, mainly because we had seen and heard a lot about the place through Instagram reels. Since we were already in Bandra, we decided to give it a try. We reached the restaurant around 9:00 PM, which is peak dinner time, and had to wait for nearly 20 minutes to get a table for four—which was understandable considering the rush.

Once seated, we ordered Chicken Tikka Masala and Chicken Tandoori as starters. The starters were okayish in taste, nothing impressive. I assume this might have been due to the restaurant working at full capacity during peak hours.

For the main course, we ordered Butter Chicken with Rumali Rotis. Unfortunately, this was the biggest disappointment of the night. I’ve had butter chicken at countless restaurants, and honestly, this was the worst butter chicken I’ve had so far—lacking flavor, richness, and balance. We also ordered Chicken Fried Rice, which again was just average.

The service experience further added to the disappointment. There was a shortage of waiters, resulting in long waiting times for food. The staff seemed extremely busy and didn’t really have the time to listen properly to customer requests or feedback.

Another thing that stood out negatively was the entertainment setup. The restaurant has two large TV screens, but they were continuously playing the same 5-minute loop video of a Japanese city. On that particular day, there was an India cricket match, and playing it on at least one screen would have kept customers engaged—especially since food service was delayed.

Overall, I personally regret choosing Jai Jawan that night and feel I could have had a better experience elsewhere. This is purely my personal opinion. You may still try it once to form your own view, but my experience was not a good one.

The freshness of the seafood here is immediately evident. Every dish feels like it has come straight from the ocean to your plate, bursting with natural flavor. The fish is perfectly cooked—tender, juicy, and never overdone—while the prawns are plump, succulent, and seasoned to perfection. Their signature preparations strike a beautiful balance between bold coastal spices and authentic home-style cooking, making each bite deeply satisfying.

What truly sets Jai Jawan apart is its consistency and authenticity. There’s no unnecessary fuss or overcomplication—just honest, well-executed dishes that showcase the richness of Mumbai’s coastal cuisine. The masalas are aromatic without being overpowering, allowing the seafood to remain the star of the show.

The service is quick, efficient, and warm, adding to the overall comfort of the dining experience. It’s the kind of place where you can relax, dig in, and leave completely content.

Whether you’re a hardcore seafood lover or simply looking to explore Mumbai’s culinary treasures, Jai Jawan is a must-visit. It’s not just a meal—it’s a celebration of fresh flavors, tradition, and the simple joy of eating great food.

featured_reviews.name: Nakul Janglay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Fresh Catch by Francis recently after hearing a lot about it and honestly came back with mixed feelings.

We tried -

Mushroom Butter Garlic was decent, nothing wrong with it, but nothing memorable either.

Bombil Rava Fry was probably the better dish of the lot. Crispy, tasty, and enjoyable.

Bangda Ambotic Curry was good, but felt like a standard Goan curry. Not something I’d go back specifically for.

Crab Meat Spicy Masala.
It was more like a regular seafood bhurji than a standout crab dish. Now where close to justifying the exorbitant price being charged.

Pomfret Hara Bhara Tawa Fry.
The biggest letdown. The fish didn’t feel particularly fresh, the taste was quite average, and the pricing for a small medium sized portion felt just too steep. For that kind of money (or even less) you can easily get a proper wholesome seafood thali elsewhere.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

If I’m spending that kind of money on seafood in Mumbai, places like Nav Chaitanya and Gajalee still set the benchmark for me in terms of flavor, consistency and value.

The dishes I ordered during my visit were Bomblivi fish fry, Prawn Rechada and a bowl of Mixed Sea food pulao.

The outcome, i was absolutely in wonderland after gorging on their food like there was no tomorrow.

The Prawn Rechada was simply outstanding to another level. The flavours, reminding me of the coastal beaches of India really gave an everlasting taste to hook onto.

The mixed seafood pulao was again another real dish that was crafted amazingly by their chefs. The homemade spice aromas were so imminent that it wasn't a surprise about finishing up the dish by myself.

Overall service and management deserves a 5/5. Food deserves a 5/5 as well .

featured_reviews.name: Riddhiman Chanda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Linking Road in Bandra is home to some of the best food in the city, and one of the best asian joints in the place is The fatty Bao. It has a modern, chic vibe crossed with a vibrant and sassy decor, perfect for a date night, or for a hangout sesh with friends.

The decor feels inspired by Malay/Singaporean cafes, with a lot of the artwork depicting the same, and it comes off pretty well. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, though the indoor seating is a bit cramped, but that's mostly fine. They do have a small bar serving the usual suspects, as well as some of their own stuff.

While I didn't get to order a large chunk of their menu, whatever I had was pretty great. Their name is definitely apt, as the baos I got were plump and pillowy, and the filling was perfect. I got the pork char siu baos, and the pork was fatty and melt in your mouth, complimented nicely by a slice of raw apple, giving it a fruity kick. Every Bao order comes with two, making it perfect for date night.

I also got their raw papaya salad, which was one of the best renditions of the dish I've eaten in Mumbai. It was tangy, sweet and spicy in just the right amounts, and wasn't just a refreshing palate cleanser, but a great meal by itself. It's also a very generous portion making it great for sharing.

The last thing I got were Chicken and asparagus dumplings, which didn't impress me as much, as I've had better dumplings in the same price range. They weren't bad but not particularly great either. The filling was generous, but it lacked in flavor. For 6 pieces, it was not the best value, and I recommend trying other dumplings, or avoiding dumplings all together.

Overall, I would rate both the Char Siu Bao and the Papaya Salad a solid 9/10, and the dumplings about a 6.5/10. Definitely go for their baos( pretty obvious given their name).

The service was fine, but they do tend to ignore the smaller tables and focus on the bigger groups, and it was also pretty busy on the day I visited. But I did see other tables also not receiving food at the proper times, so I'd rate the service a little lower, like a 6/10. Definitely could do with some improvement.

The Fatty Bao definitely ticks a lot of the boxes, though they do miss a little bit in their service, and cocktail variety, though I did not have the opportunity to try it. However, they more than make up for it with their snazzy decor and contemporary vibe, along with some pretty great food. I highly recommend checking the place out if you're out shopping in Linking Road and need to grab some lunch or dinner. You're definitely gonna be leaving a happy and fatty bao when you're done.

Final rating- 8.5/10, definitely recommend.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind Lunch Home,  Pali Naka,  Bandra (west)

Jai Hind is a brightest shining star of the galaxy of coastal cuisine restaurants in Mumbai.  With the few branches spread across the city,  this branch at Bandra,  Pali Naka is their first branch.  The other one is on the Linking Road, which seems to be rather spacious and well furnished.  But as a foodie, my hunt is always for a 'Value for money'  restaurants with excellent quality and quantity and this desire of mime gets fulfilled only in humble homely restaurants.  This branch at Pali Naka has been renovated recently and has only five tables in all.  I recommend to reserve a table in the evening as its a very old and famous restaurant in the area and gets filled quite soon.

The list of dishes we ordered :

1.  Patra Ni Macchi (Basa)
2. Bombil Thali
3. Chicken Sukka Thali

Let me begin with the most yummiest first. The chicken sukka was simply top quality stuff made with supreme perfection. It was creamy with great blend of masalas and literally made us lick our fingers till the end.  The chicken pieces were one of the softest and well marinated ones I ever had.  The Bombil was crispy and crunchy on the outside and soft juicy within. The soul kadi (pink broth)  was thick and made with actual coconut milk.  The texture of the chapatis were homely and rice was soft, fresh and well cooked.

Patra Ni Macchi was steamed to ultimate perfection,  which retained the original flavour of the soft melting Basa fish.  The green stuffing on it was blend of spicy and sour.

Over all,  A must visit restaurant..
Staff is helpful

featured_reviews.name: Pereira Gynel
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place has such an amazing tropical ambience. You are welcomed by soulful Goan music, and the vibe is relaxed and unhurried. The servers don’t rush you, making it a perfect spot to truly enjoy your meal.

Mr. Merwin, the manager, took great care of us, and our servers Sonia and Edwin were humble, polite, and very prompt, obliging us with every request.

The food is unlike anything you’ve tasted.. authentic Goan cuisine rooted deeply in the culture and spices of Goa. Every dish is beautifully presented, with thoughtful plating that elevates the experience without being overdone. The cutlery, plates, and glassware are aesthetically pleasing and enhance the dining experience, without robbing you of quantity. Portions are generous and satisfying.

From the big plates, we had the Traditional Pork Sorpatel with rice, Goan-style chilli chicken, and Surmai fish curry rice. The sorpatel was so authentic it made my mum emotional...it brought back memories of old friends who had cooked traditional pork dishes in her younger days. The Goan-style chilli chicken was the standout dish of the afternoon...smooth, succulent, and packed with a powerful flavour punch. The surmai fish curry rice felt like something an old granny had made, warm, comforting, and soulful.

From the small plates, we tried the Goan fried chicken with spicy mayo...six generous boneless strips, made to order, pairing perfectly with lime and the spicy mayo. The grilled squid stuffed with crab was outstanding, with the masala truly stealing the show. The prawn balchao masala stuffed forminhas crispy tarts were tangy and well-made; while not my personal favourite, they were only overshadowed by stronger dishes. The tender coconut and raw mango salad was light, tropical, refreshing, and beautifully balanced.

For drinks, we had the Coconut Boy Refresher, Kokum Spritz, and Tamarind Trails. These are not your usual cocktails... Goan spices and flavours take centre stage, and an open mind is needed to fully enjoy them.

Coconut Boy truly lives up to its promise of 'fresh' and delivers an experience that transports you straight to Goa. Highly recommended even if you’re simply looking for some relaxed downtime with exceptional food and service.

featured_reviews.review_text:
AMBIENCE:

Despite being located at a busy intersection, the instant you come inside, you are taken to a tranquil and unexpectedly quiet environment. Amidst the dim lights and décor paying ode to the Goan theme, what we appreciated the most was the ample open space to move around and even dance (which our daughter did multiple times throughout the night).

FOOD:
Vegetable Cheese Rissois: Though the classic Portuguese fried pastry is usually filled with meat, we tried the vegetarian version and were not disappointed. It starts with a crumbly-soft bite which leads to a minced vegetables mixed with cheese that definitely melts in your mouth.

Mapusa Market toast with Cheese & Green Chilli: Coconut boys take on the chilli cheese toast with a twist. On first look it’s just your average cheese chilli toast, but one bite into it and you hit a tangy punch which took us by surprise…. It was mango aachaar! ‘Who would’ave thunk?’ This dish did have some mixed opinions!

Choris Chilli Fry: Choriz tossed with chilli, onion, tomato teamed up with warm, fluffy poee… we absolutely left licking our fingers. Would have gone for round two but there was more to be relished on the menu.

Grilled Squid Stuffed with Crab: A host suggestion that we absolutely jumped at the mention of! Crab meat tossed in Recheado, stuffed into a squid & grilled… a lot of effort goes into this. Hints of spice married with the sweetness of the crab meat and the bite of squid… a messy meal you must try at least once! Definitely big brownie points for the squid NOT being chewy.

Mushroom & vegetables slow cooked with Xacuti masala: A medley of steamed veggies (Mushroom, carrot, potato, cauliflower) tossed in a Xacuti gravy. You have an option of Poee or steamed rice to accompany it and we went with the latter. We requested them to hold back the spice a bit for our toddler & it’s wholesome, earthy, slightly-sweet coconut-ty broth was welcomed with a smack of the lips.

Serradura: This simple pudding can go awry in so many ways… And believe me, we've tasted some absolute disasters. But coconut boy absolutely nailed-it! The crumbly, biscuit dust alternated with fluffy, light whipped cream was what we devoured at the end of a great meal. Not too sweet, not too dense… just perfect.

Service: The service undoubtedly elevated our entire experience! We had Siddhesh giving us amazing recommendations and making sure we had everything we needed. Akbar stopped by with some fantastic banter, and last but not least, Faustin, whom our daughter adored and sat with virtually the entire dinner, allowing us to savour every bite!

SUMMING UP: If you love Goan food, it’s definitely an experience you do not want to miss. Right from the décor to the service, it’s comfy, cozy and warm. The cost is a bit on the higher end but the quality and flavors are worth every penny.

featured_reviews.name: Hania
featured_reviews.review_text:
Peach Ice Tea
Peach Iced Tea is a refreshing burst of flavor in every sip.

Kalimiri Cheddar Broccoli
From the moment the dish arrives, the vibrant green of the broccoli is contrasted beautifully by the creamy richness of the cheddar cheese, infused with the subtle yet captivating warmth of kalimiri (black pepper). The aroma is inviting—cheesy, slightly spicy, and earthy.The broccoli retains a nice crunch, providing a fresh, earthy base to the dish. The cheddar is indulgently smooth, delivering a familiar, comforting creaminess. But what sets this dish apart is the kalimiri. The black pepper’s spice gently lingers, balancing the richness of the cheese with a subtle heat. The tender yet slightly crisp broccoli pairs wonderfully with the velvety melted cheddar. Perfect for those looking for something familiar with a hint of spice. However, the spice of cardamom was overpowered and sat on tongue, so every bite was full of cardamom, which made the next dishes taste like it too.

Tiranga Kofte
Visually, the Tiranga Kofte presents itself well, with three distinct layers symbolizing the colours of the Indian flag. The presentation is appealing and sets high expectations for a flavourful experience. However, the dish's appearance slightly outweighs its taste. The kofte has a decent blend of spices, though the flavours don’t quite come together as cohesively as expected. Each layer brings something different—the green layer offers a mild herbiness, the white layer is a bit bland, and the orange section has a touch of heat. However, the balance between them feels uneven, with the spices not blending as harmoniously as they should.
Since the appetizer had cardamom hint which was overpowering, the outer layer green part of kofta also felt it had cardamom which wasn’t pleasant on tongue.

Amritsari Kulcha
The Amritsari-styled kulcha is a delightful treat. Each bite offers a perfect blend of crispy exterior and soft, flavorful interior. The traditional stuffing of spiced potatoes and herbs is well-seasoned, providing a hearty and satisfying taste

Lachha Paratha
The Lachha Paratha is a standout with its perfectly layered, crispy texture. Each bite reveals a delightful combination of flaky. Though they forgot to add butter because it was some miscommunication, It was perfect size not big not small.

Tadkewali Dal
Tadkewali Dal delivers a heartwarming, flavorful experience. The smoky aroma from the tadka (tempering) hits you immediately, preparing your senses for a rich and comforting dish. The lentils are cooked to perfection—and well-spiced. The tadka of ghee, cumin, garlic, and chilies adds depth, bringing a savory warmth to every bite. Each spoonful is a harmonious blend of velvety dal and robust, fragrant spices. It’s a perfect dish for anyone seeking bold yet balanced flavors in a simple, soul-satisfying homely meal.

Jeera rice
Jeera Rice is simplicity at its finest. The delicate aroma of cumin wafts through each grain, giving the rice a warm, earthy fragrance. The cumin seeds add a subtle crunch and a toasted, nutty flavor that complements the perfectly cooked, fluffy rice.

Halwa (Complementary)
Rich and buttery, each spoonful melts in your mouth, releasing a wave of sweetness that’s perfectly balanced with hints of cardamom. The texture is smooth yet slightly grainy, with bursts of flavor from the roasted nuts scattered throughout.

Hospitality
The hospitality at this restaurant is exceptional. From the moment we walked in, the staff was warm, attentive, and welcoming. They ensured every detail was taken care of, making us feel comfortable and valued throughout the meal. Service was prompt, yet never rushed, with the team showing genuine care in their recommendations and interactions. Their professionalism, combined with friendly smiles, truly elevated our experience. Ashish and Prasad served great hospitality to us.

Ambience
The ambience of Rasoi strikes the perfect balance between luxury and comfort. The decor is elegant yet welcoming, with soft lighting and tasteful accents that create a warm, inviting atmosphere

featured_reviews.name: Sandeep Damle
featured_reviews.review_text: Went here on a Sunday for lunch without any reservation, and we immediately got seating by the live sushi counter, which was surprisingly cozy. The ambience of the place is simple but pretty, just how a japanese restaurant should be. We tried a sushi, gyoza, yakitori chicken and udon noodles, and although everything tasted great, nothing really stood out as outstanding. The thing is that these days there are several multi-cuisine/asian restaurants who also serve good authentic japanese dishes, which thus reduces the novelty factor of an authentic japanese-only restaurant, although the menu is wider here. The service here is excellent, and the prices are also reasonable. Valet parking is available. Overall there's no negative about the place and it's definitely worth visiting.

featured_reviews.name: shreyash gavankar
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Izumi Bandra recently and had a good overall experience. The food was tasty, well-presented, and had an authentic Japanese feel. That said, the quality of the food makes up for it to an extent. A good spot to try if you enjoy Japanese cuisine and don’t mind spending a little extra. featured_reviews.review_text:
Been here on multiple occasions and it's always our go to spot for sushi in Bandra.

They have a fantastic selection of cocktails to choose from and we always go with the hamachi, unagi, chutoro nigiri/maki along with 1-2 robata grills (tenderloin and snapper are really good). The sushi is always fresh and service is pretty quick. The staff is also very friendly and were able to accomodate us even without any reservation.

featured_reviews.name: aakruti dave
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Izumi, Bandra — a popular spot with good food options and a lively vibe. The place has ample seating, but it was quite full when we visited on a Sunday afternoon.
We tried the crispy edamame avocado — the portion size was good. The rice was slightly sticky, but other than that, the sushi was tasty. We also had a fresh orange juice, which was refreshing and good.
The staff is very polite, smiling, and welcoming, which adds to the overall experience.
Overall, a nice place to explore for good food and a buzzing atmosphere.

featured_reviews.name: CorporateNomad
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent Ramen. Service was average. And decor was good and minimal.
What mattered was what we went for - Soul food and got that. Ordered 3 different ramen and all were excellent. The pork and chicken broth were better than the vegetarian one.
We just walked in and got a table without an issue. Reservation was not done as the numbers were always engaged which we tried for last 3 days.
Have to make more trips for the Sushi and Robata.

featured_reviews.name: Indrajit Advani
featured_reviews.review_text: Having visited Kuuraku a week earlier, this was the second Japanese restaurant in Mumbai to positively surprise us. The smoked crispy pork belly was not too salty (as is often the case with pork in India) and it was indeed tender though it was a shame that it was doused in mayonnaise. The rock shrimp and squid tempura was a generous portion though the batter was just a little too heavy and somewhat disguised the taste of the prawn and squid. We had a prawn okomiyaki, which was very enjoyable though I would have liked to have the option of no bonito flakes, and a little less sauce, that again disguised the taste of the pancake. The chicken tsukune was perfect and one of the highlights of the meal, perhaps bettered only by the buta burra with enoki mushroom, which was divine. The spider roll was another generous portion item and quite good again. Having enjoyed the food so much we went full blast and ordered one desser each. The black sesame ice cream was pretty good without perhaps the subtle flavour of some of the best that we've had but it was certainly better than the warabi mochi, which was a limp disappointment. But the hit of the three was definitely the fuji tropica. Once it arrived we didn't know what to expect - but it was fantastic - reminding us of 'dippin' dots'. All in all a very enjoyable meal although at RS8,700 it wasn't cheap.

featured_reviews.name: Sav
featured_reviews.review_text:
I crave for authentic japnese restaurants with fresh high quality meat and in one line, this is it. The food was absolutely the best authentic quality of japanese one could hope to get in India. It was not perfect by any means yet I could not ask for more considering how atrocious some other places can be.
The cocktails were all for a sweet pallet but the match foam was incredible, a delicacy. The Katsu curry, which I have tried many of was most certainly one of the best. I know now that everytime I travel to Bombay, I shall come by here to feast.

Wine menu could be improved for by glass for such a restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Prakash Dhalwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambience & Parking: ⭐⭐⭐
Decent vibe, though the seating was a bit uncomfortable. We pre-booked our table via Zomato. Valet is available, but note that they park your car on the street. A quick shoutout to the bathrooms—very clean and hygienic!

Service: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Excellent. The staff was incredibly quick, efficient, and responsive throughout the meal.

Food & Drinks:
✅ Truffle Salmon Sushi - Absolute perfection with amazing flavor. (5/5)
✅ Egg Fried Rice - Flawless, classic taste, and good portion size. (5/5)
✅ Avocado Cream Cheese Sushi - A great, creamy option. (4/5)
✅ Chicken and Chilli Oil Dumplings - Nice flavor with a good spicy kick. (4/5)
❌ Chicken Spring Roll - Pretty average, nothing memorable. (3/5)
❌ Lemon Ice Tea & Jade Mojito - Both felt a bit uninspiring for the price. (3/5)
⭐Truffle Salmon Sushi - Easily the standout dish of the entire meal!

Pricing & Value:
Our bill was around ₹4,500 for 3 people. Given the good portion sizes and quality of the mains, it felt fair.

💡Pro Tip:
Pre-book on Zomato! They have a 25% discount running, but slots are limited.

A solid spot with remarkably fast service and excellent sushi, though it's held back slightly by average drinks and stiff seating.

Would I Recommend It?
Depends (Definitely go if you can grab the Zomato discount and stick to their top-tier sushi).

Must Try:
Truffle Salmon Sushi, Egg Fried Rice

Skip:
Chicken Spring Roll, Jade Mojito

featured_reviews.name: chanakya dhiman
featured_reviews.review_text:
An Unforgettable Asian Dining Experience in the Heart of Khar!
If you're looking for a restaurant that delivers on every front — breathtaking interiors, extraordinary food, and an experience that lingers long after the meal — look no further than PF Chang's, Khar. This place is an absolute gem, and my recent visit left me completely blown away.

The moment you step inside PF Chang's, you're transported into a world of stunning elegance. The interiors are nothing short of spectacular — a seamless blend of contemporary design and rich Asian-inspired aesthetics. From the dramatic lighting and intricate décor to the beautifully curated artwork and warm, inviting tones, every corner of this restaurant is Instagram-worthy. The space feels luxurious yet comfortable, making it perfect for a romantic date night, a family celebration, or a fun outing with friends. It's the kind of place where the ambiance alone is worth the visit.

Now, let's talk about the food — because PF Chang's truly takes Asian cuisine to another level. The menu is a love letter to the flavors of Asia, and every dish we tried was an absolute revelation. The dishes were bursting with bold, authentic flavors, perfectly balanced with the right amount of spice, sweetness, and umami. The portions were generous, the ingredients were fresh, and the presentation was exquisite. From the starters to the mains, each plate was crafted with care and culinary finesse. This is Asian food at its absolute finest!

The staff were warm, professional, and genuinely passionate about making your dining experience special. The team was attentive without being intrusive, and their knowledge of the menu made ordering an enjoyable experience in itself.
Overall, PF Chang's in Khar, Mumbai is a world-class dining destination that truly lives up to its global reputation. It's not just a meal — it's an experience. If you haven't visited yet, you're seriously missing out. This is one restaurant I will be returning to again and again without hesitation.
Highly recommended — a perfect 10/10! 🥢✨

featured_reviews.name: Mohak Khullar
featured_reviews.review_text: Mumbai has really good chinese food, so the bar was high. But sadly PF chang's didn't fully live up to it. The dynamite shrimp was the best part of my meal. Other than that, the noodles were nothing special and the cottage cheese in black bean sauce was not spicy enough for me. If you are thinking of coming here I would recommend you to eat the starters only and skip the dynamite broccoli.

The restaurant ambience was amazing, though I did find the beverages slightly overpriced. The pan-fried prawn dumplings were a bit bland, and the chilli oil lacked flavour. That said, the rest of the dishes were excellent, and the chocolate cake was absolutely amazing. A special thank you to the head chef for taking our feedback positively and suggesting some great dishes.

The food was enjoyable; the Bao was delicious, and the rice was cooked to perfection. Service was attentive, and the air conditioning kept the place comfortable.

The ambience was great, and I would definitely recommend booking a table in advance, especially on weekends, to avoid waiting. I’ll be adding the bill (soon) with dish names so newcomers can get an idea of what to try.

featured_reviews.name: Ninad joshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Whenever I intended to travel to Mumbai, we always make an effort to discover new dining; this time, we chose to visit P.F. Chang's in Khar.

On Saturday evening, our cousins planned to go to this venue, so we made a reservation through Zomato.

After we settled in, one of my cousins started placing the order. We enjoyed the following dishes:
- Orange Chicken
- Original Dynamite Shrimp
- Avocado Cream Cheese Roll
- Aburi Salmon Roll
- Handmade Chicken Dumplings
- Pan-Fried Crab Wonton
- Wok Charred Chicken
- Hand-Folded Crab Wontons
- Signature Lo Mein
- Singapore Street Noodles
- Sticky Toffee Pudding
- Chicken in Black Bean Sauce
- Hot Garlic Sichuan Chicken

**Must Try**
1. Orange Chicken; this dish was exceptionally delicious, and the flavor of the orange was outstanding.
2. The Original Dynamite Shrimp was delightful in taste, featuring a blend of creamy, spicy mayonnaise, sriracha, and sweet chili sauce.
3. The Handmade Chicken Dumplings were also quite tasty.

**Recommendation**
Both sushi rolls were delicious, and I would recommend them:
1. Avocado Cream Cheese Roll
2. Aburi Salmon Roll

The service was prompt, and the highlight was that every dish arrived on time. The soothing background music contributed to a relaxing atmosphere.

Overall, it was a wonderful experience for us, and I would certainly recommend this place.

Service is sharp, portions are generous, and the menu is packed with bold, authentic Pan-Asian flavors done right. If you love food that excites your palate and a vibe that elevates your night, this place deserves a spot on your list. Must visit.

Seafood lovers will be in heaven with their wide selection of fresh, well-cooked options. The food presentation is top-notch, making every dish a visual treat before you even take a bite. The ambience is super cute and cozy, perfect for a casual date or dinner with friends. Despite the high quality, the prices are surprisingly reasonable. featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
📍 Kuai Kitchen – Khar West, Mumbai
🍱 Location: Shop No. 3/4, Mangal Bhavna, Khar Pali Rd, Khar West, Mumbai 400052
If you're a fan of sushi, dim sum, and pan-Asian cuisine, Kuai Kitchen is the place to be! The ambience here is aesthetic and welcoming, with both indoor and outdoor dining options that make it a perfect spot for a cozy meal or a catch-up with friends.
We started off with some refreshing mocktails — I tried the Martini mocktail, which was super refreshing and full of flavor. My brother went for the Panda Passion, and not only did it taste amazing, but the presentation was on point too!
Here’s what we ordered and absolutely loved:
🍤 Dynamite Prawns – perfectly crispy and packed with flavor.
🥟 Spicy Chicken Dumplings – delicious, with a rich, flavorful filling and great presentation.
🍣 Volcano Prawn Tempura Roll Sushi – visually stunning and tasted just as good as it looked.
🍗 Chicken with Chilli Oil and Spring Onion – bold flavors with a nice kick.
🍚 Blue Butter Japanese Fried Rice (Chicken) – cooked to perfection, flavorful, and unique in taste.
And finally, to end on a sweet note:
🍫 Labubu Chocolate Bao – a warm, gooey dessert bao that was absolutely mouthwatering!
✨ The service was top-notch. The staff were attentive and helpful, and the manager personally guided us through the menu. Every dish was presented beautifully, and the quality was consistent throughout.
💯 Overall: 10/10 Experience
Highly recommended for all lovers of Thai, Asian, sushi, and dim sum. Add this place to your food bucket list — you won't regret it!

featured_reviews.name: aditya mathur
featured_reviews.review_text:
FAKE HYPE. AVOID visit. Very disappointed. Nothing special atall. Just a mediocre pan Asia joint . Lets get straight to it. Came here as i read good reviews online but sadly it was all wrong.
We were a party of 10 who went here on a Saturday night.
Cons :
1. No valet when we arrived. Had to look for parking for 15 mins.
2. Less than enthusiastic staff and thats putting lightly.
3. Small place so getting a seating inside might be difficult.
4. Lotus stem and teriyaki bao were soo sweet that it felt like eating desert. This was conveyed to the management for feedback.
5. Tatse and portion of the dishes do not justify the its cost. Too steep for the kind of mideocre food available.
6. Steamed rice was undercooked and left untouched. We had given up by this time and resorted to looking elsewhere for dinner party 2 .
7. No alcohol. Alcohol would have helped in stuffing down some of the itmes we ordered or atleast numb our taste buds enough to appreciate the food.
Pros :
1. Ambience is neat and cosy.
2. The sushi was very well made and we all enjoyed it.
3. The menu is well curated with good variety of both veg and non veg options.
I dont know if this was a one off case or our choice of items was poor or the staff was overwhelmed on a Saturday night or was it just the normal standard here but the fact remains that we were truly disappointed 😔 by the experience.

We stayed at Le Sutra Hotel in Khar, and Out of the Blue Café, located within the hotel, was definitely a highlight of our visit. The café has both an open-air seating area and an indoor air-conditioned section, offering a comfortable and cozy experience.

We really enjoyed our breakfast here. On Saturday, we experienced their jazz night which had a lively crowd, soothing live music, and a great atmosphere. The food was excellent. Their fondue and sizzlers are highly recommended.

On Sunday, we tried their unlimited brunch which was truly delightful. There was a live bar counter, fresh fusion omelettes, pasta counters, and a wide selection of a la carte dishes to choose from. Being non-vegetarians, we appreciated the variety and taste of everything served.

If you love desserts, make sure to try the Blue Gourmet selections, which are beautifully presented and taste just as good.

The overall vibe of the place is warm and welcoming. Located in Khar, it attracts a good crowd and makes for a perfect weekend outing.

featured_reviews.review_text: Truly one of the best in the business. While they have several locations, this specific branch stands out as the finest. We ate way too much, ordering in the app is great for foreigners that do not know all the items. Good mix of veggie and meat options from all different cuisines. We had an absolute blast.

featured_reviews.review_text:

The ambiance is rustic. We felt our table lacked lights. They also have outdoor seating. It was a match day so of course the match was going on along with preparation for the night event.

The service was a bit slow but the server was really impressive with his suggestions, one extra star for him!

featured_reviews.name: Atharva Rao
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing time at Social tonight. Great energy, solid crowd, amazing music and the food absolutely delivered. But the real highlight was Munawar.

One of the most attentive, warm and genuinely professional waiters I’ve come across in a long time. He handled everything effortlessly even during peak rush hours, kept checking in at the right moments without being intrusive, gave great recommendations and made the entire experience feel premium and comfortable.

Hospitality like this genuinely changes the vibe of a place. Staff members like Munawar are a huge reason people come back. Massive respect to him and the entire team at Social Khar for maintaining such a lively yet welcoming atmosphere.

featured_reviews.name: Apurva Prajapati
featured_reviews.review_text: We went there on Friday night and the experience was great! The DJ was superb! Also, there were many partners of the DJ and they were also good performers. To add a cherry on the cake, Prince Narula also visited the place at the same time and rapped on a song. We loved it. Enjoyed the place. Keep up guys!

featured_reviews.name: Nawaal Sunke
featured_reviews.review_text: Social is generally known for its reliable food, lively atmosphere, and enjoyable outings with friends. However, my recent visit to the Khar location unfortunately fell short of expectations. The quality of the food was disappointing across the board, with several dishes falling flat. I suspect the chicken may have been stale, as it didn't taste fresh. Overall, it was a subpar experience.

featured_reviews.name: Sidharth Jhawar
featured_reviews.review_text: This vibrant establishment offers a delightful dining experience with its energetic atmosphere.  The menu boasts a selection of incredibly tasty dishes, all offered at very reasonable prices.  Every bite is a burst of flavor, showcasing fresh ingredients and culinary expertise.  The ambiance is truly captivating, creating a warm and inviting space for any occasion. Their non alcoholic beverages were a blast. I especially recommend their spiced guavava juice. The service was slightly slow, especially for Indian thali. Their chinese thali was great tasting and covered a variety of different elements. I highly recommend experiencing this gem for yourself.

featured_reviews.name: abhishek yenji
featured_reviews.review_text:
The service here is extremely poor. The waitstaff seriously need training in basic customer service. When asked about the menu, they respond with an attitude, simply telling customers to check the app or scanner. Yet, even after placing an order, we were twice informed that certain items were unavailable.

The food is decent but lacks essentials—no dips served with wings or burgers. Portions are also noticeably small, likely to make the menu seem more “exclusive.”

Service Charge: They automatically add a 10% tip, which they absolutely do not deserve. We requested its removal, and they complied. If they refuse, don’t hesitate to call the authorities.

Would not recommend this place based on service alone.

The place feels a bit overpriced considering the overall ambiance and portion sizes. Still, if you’re in the area and craving some pan-Asian flavors, it’s worth a visit — just be ready for a slightly premium bill.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik K. Mody
featured_reviews.review_text:
Nom Nom is such a vibe!

The ambience really stands out! That warm, dim lighting sets the perfect mood for an intimate dinner without feeling too “try-hard.” It’s the kind of place where you naturally slow down, settle in, and actually enjoy the evening.
The food, overall, was really good and definitely amps up the experience. That said, I’d love to see a wider variety of sushi and noodle dishes on the menu. The bao bun was a bit on the chewy side, and the filling-to-bun ratio felt slightly off (could’ve used more filling). The silken tofu, though was an absolute standout. It genuinely melted in the mouth and was a wow dish, even if I wish the portion was a little more generous. The peach iced tea was perfect. Dessert-wise, the mango sticky rice could’ve been better, it felt a bit like mango purée with pieces and rice, missing that coconut-y flavour and crunch (both of which are not very difficult to crack).
Definitely a spot I’d come back to (and happily recommend) when I’m in the mood for a relaxed, date-night style dinner.

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Malaika Arora’s newest restaurant in Khar so let me rate everything I ate at Sweeney. Goat cheese croquettes with chilli honey - Very cheesy, soft and you’ll like if you like different kinds of cheese. 9/10.
Chilli butter garlic prawns - While the flavours packed a punch, it would have been better with a thicker gravy. 7/10.
Chimichurri Prawn Risotto - Quite a unique take. The prawns were spicy and nice and the risotto paired well. 8/10.
Krawpow Chicken - Pair this with Chilli Rice. This chopped chicken gravy feels like your regular comfort Chinese food but gourmet. 8/10.
Mango Sticky Rice Creme Brulee - This is supposed to be their star dessert and it does live up. The mango quality is insanely good. 9/10.
Sweeney resembles a cozy cottage with a homegrown mango tree and dimlly lit corners. It’s got a great vibe and is a good pick for dates or girly meals. If you love Thai and European cuisines, save this spot.

The ambience of the restaurant is chic and inviting, perfect for a calm dinner. Staff members were attentive and made us feel very comfortable. Everything from the lighting to the music added to the experience. I would definitely order this again on my next visit.

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh Harisinghani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Newly opened restaurant with another branch in Goregaon east.

The interiors are beautifully done, with Marathi songs playing in the background, adds to the authentic vibe. A special mention to Abhishek Prabhu, the manager, who was extremely helpful and guided us through the menu.

We were welcomed with papads served alongside three sides – thecha, green chutney, and masala oil – all packed with flavour.

The Pomfret in Banana Leaf was a highlight: steamed in green masala and then finished in a banana leaf. The fish was fresh and tasted amazing, especially when paired with the masala oil.

We also tried the Mutton Kolhapuri Thali, which came with pandra rassa, tambda rassa, kheema, and Kolhapuri gravy, along with bhakri, masala bhaat, and salad. A hearty and satisfying meal.

Although we initially skipped dessert, Abhishek insisted we try their freshly made in-house ice creams in jackfruit, guava, and coconut jaggery flavours — and they were absolutely out of this world! To our surprise, he didn’t even charge us for them despite our insistence.

We paid around ₹2000 for two people. It’s slightly on the higher side, but the food, service, and overall experience made it worth it. Definitely visiting again!

featured_reviews.name: Vivian Nguyen
featured_reviews.review_text:
My Marathi friend recommended me to come here and oh my… it was insanity. I already came in not hungry, but I cleared everything. After the meal, even though I was so full, I was still missing the taste of the meal I just had. On my walk back, I could taste the breath of the best meal I’ve ever had in India (& I’ve had a lot of dishes) I didn’t want to brush my teeth so I could savor the taste (but I did brush my teeth)

When I arrived, the owner told me (not verbatim), “Apologies for the smoke, because of the gas shortage, we are using coal fire to cook.” It’s a terrible situation, for sure; a lot of restaurants have been suffering from the gas shortage… but I guiltily admit I was even more excited to try the food because nothing elevates a dish more than the taste a coal brings.

The ice cream was next level, too. All made in house, real fruit, no preservatives. Left to right: coconut jaggery, guava, custard apple, and they were all amazing.

A lot of times in India, restaurants/accommodations will ask me to write a good review for them. This is 100% an organic review, unprompted. I just needed to tell the world how good this mutton thali was!!

The service was kind, attentive, and exceptional on top of everything out. I’m flying out of India on Sunday, and I am already grieving the loss of access to one of the most delicious meals I’ve ever eaten.

featured_reviews.name: Rahil Kotadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place by the Bawa Hotels Group is a good option if you’re in the mood for Punjabi food, just don’t walk in expecting completely authentic flavours. The taste is slightly toned down, but if you set your expectations right, you’ll actually enjoy the food.

The menu is quite well done, and the meal box options are a big plus. Makes ordering super easy without having to overthink or pick too many individual items.

Their parathas are definitely worth trying—served nicely with curd. Do ask for white butter separately though, as it’s not given by default and really makes a difference. The lassi is a must-have here, easily one of the better things on the menu.

Also, a special mention for the Kalimiri chicken shorba. It’s not on the menu, but if they have it, don’t miss it—it’s genuinely very good.

Ambience is nice and comfortable, so no complaints there. Service, however, is quite slow and needs serious improvement, which can get a bit frustrating.

Parking is another issue—since it’s close to the railway station, the area is always crowded and finding a spot is tough. Better to plan that in advance.

Overall, a good place to chill and enjoy a meal, as long as you’re okay overlooking the service and parking hassles.

featured_reviews.name: Suhani Mendonsa
featured_reviews.review_text:
Khar just got a delicious new reason to celebrate with Bawa Kitchen opening its doors this Lohri! From the first bite, it felt like a true Punjabi feast — rich, soulful and full of festive warmth. My absolute favourites were their creamy butter chicken, soft and flavourful chhole kulcha, and the super refreshing lassi that perfectly balanced the spices. Every dish tasted like it was made with love and tradition. If you’re craving authentic Punjabi flavours with a celebratory twist, this is the place to be — go check it out and treat yourself to a hearty, happy meal!
And yes, my festive Lohri fit was specially curated — can’t wait to share it with you all soon!

The food was on point - I ordered Ajwaini Rawas for my appetizer and it came with this spicy tandoori salad (think Thai Som Yum but not as sweet or wet) and Green chutney which was the perfect accompaniment. For my mains I got the Mutton Beliram (don’t why it’s called that) which was nice and spicy, along with a roomali roti. I’d recommend ordering a naan instead - lots of very moorish sauce to lap up! Got some Jal Jeera with soda to wash it down (not sure about the boondi). Finished off with some Gulabjamun - there is definitely a hint of “Gulab” there! And just look at those soft, pillowy, inviting mounds. 😆

Overall Bawa Kitchen echoes the punjabi ethos when it comes to food. It’s definitely a place I’d recommend and visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Subodh Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Dined here this evening based on several recommendations. While the quality of the main course (butter chicken & rice & Wok fried crab) was very good and clearly reflects the skill of the kitchen team, the overall experience was unfortunately impacted by poor service.

The staff appeared inattentive, and one item, which is one of the signatures recommended by the staff ( king prawn) was served incorrectly / extremely cold which was disappointing. Basic service standards and attention to detail were lacking throughout the visit.

With improved staff training and better guest engagement, this restaurant has strong potential, as the food itself is commendable. I hope to see improvements in service on future visits.

Visited this place with my ex-colleagues, and to be honest, The vibe of the place is great for spending time with family.

We ordered quite a few dishes including prawns masala fry, bombil masala, bombil rawa fry, grilled pomfret, crab lollipop, chicken, and finally prawns biryani.

Talking about the food, the crab lollipop was interesting. It obviously felt like frozen food, but the taste was still good. However, most of the seafood dishes were a little disappointing for us. The fish dishes were not spicy enough and lacked that strong flavor we were expecting. The stuffed pomfret was just okay-okay and felt more like boiled fish rather than properly fried.

We also ordered a chicken dish and specifically requested it to be spicy, but unfortunately, it turned out a bit sweet, and none of us really liked it.

But the highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns biryani. It was really, really good and honestly the best dish we had there.

Overall, the ambience and company made the experience enjoyable, but food-wise, only a few dishes really stood out for us.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Our go-to family dinner spot for any and every occasion. From small celebrations to casual dinners, this place has always been our first choice. Over time we’ve tried almost everything on the menu, and every visit somehow turns into another food memory with family.

If there are two dishes I would recommend to anyone visiting, it has to be the Bombil Fry and Peri Peri Bombil. They are easily my brother’s and my absolute favourites perfectly crispy, full of flavour, and something we end up ordering almost every single time.

And no meal here feels complete without the Kokum Sarbat or Kokum Soda. That refreshing, tangy punch of flavour just balances the seafood so well and makes the whole experience even better.

Good food, great flavours, and the comfort of family dinners this place truly feels special to us. Easily one of the best seafood restaurants and definitely a spot we’ll keep coming back to.

This was the final restaurant I attended on my trip and a great place to end on.

Unfortunately at the time of our attendance the A/C was not in working order which the manager/owner advised on prior to entering, however we still went in as they had fans going on.

Didn't plan to eat a lot but to take in the delights on offer as again this was a place recommended.

We were given good information by the manager on some of the dishes and on ordering the food arrived after a short time. temperatures were on point and flavours were amazing. The prawn starters were so good, especially the Prawns Garlic Butter, so much so we ordered another tray. I also order the Mutton Chops Ghee Roast and as it sat in front of me my mouth was watering. Spice level on this was perfect, had a nice little kick but was really enjoyable and not in a overpowering way. I found that the chop may have been slightly overdone to my liking, however this didn't take the enjoyment away from it.

The meals ordered were enjoyed by everyone in the party which also included children (they really enjoyed the Prawns Garlic Butter). Pricing of the meals and overall was very reasonable and this place is worth a visit if you have never been. I will look to return here again if I visit Mumbai again.

What we ordered:

Mutton Kheema Pattice: A deep-fried snack with mutton kheema stuffed in mashed potato – absolutely delicious!

Bharleli Bombil: Bombil fish stuffed with green chutney and fried. Tasty, but next time I’d prefer plain bombil with chutney on the side.

Tisrya Kalwan: A unique and flavorful clams gravy that paired perfectly with wade.

The total bill for two came to ₹1400. Prices are on the higher side, but the menu is full of interesting and authentic CKP veg/non-veg dishes. Was this the best Mahrashtrian cuisine? No, not really but it's worth trying!
